questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What challenge does video add compared with single images?

choices.text: Video can never be generated by AI tools, so it is always real footage from a camera

questions.intro: Generated and AI-edited VIDEO can show people, places and events that never happened, or change real footage. Video adds a challenge that single images lack: CONSISTENCY OVER TIME. Check frame to frame: do faces, clothes, objects and backgrounds stay the same? Do hands, text and logos warp? Does lip movement match the words? Does movement obey ordinary physics, such as objects not passing through each other? When a video uses a SYNTHETIC PRESENTER, an AI-generated person or avatar, tell viewers clearly, for example with an on-screen label or a note in the description.

sections.skill: Compare video consistency with continuity in movies

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What is the continuity job in movies?

choices.text: Keeping details the same between shots
Writing the music that plays during the final scenes of the movie for the audience

questions.correct_answer: Keeping details the same between shots
questions.intro: Movie crews have a job called CONTINUITY: making sure that if an actor's coffee cup is half full in one shot, it is not suddenly full in the next, and that a bandage stays on the same arm. Viewers notice these slips. Generated video has continuity problems too, often more of them: a necklace disappears, a sign changes words, a person's hair changes length between moments.

sections.skill: Handle subtle edits and context in video

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: A real video has one word changed by AI. Why can this matter?
questions.intro: Some edits are subtle: a real video with one changed word, a background replaced, or a crowd made larger. Even honest edits can mislead if context is removed, such as a clip cut so a person seems to say the opposite. When you publish edited or generated video, disclose the changes that matter, keep the original footage, and never put words in a real person's mouth. If a synthetic presenter looks like a real person, you need that person's consent.
